description: Benchmark prompts for ChatQEC's LightStim integration — covers the qec_circuit_build MCP tool (toric/color/BB/PQRM circuit construction) and the ingested LightStim paper (arXiv:2604.21472) + curated docs (docs/api/, skills/). Not run in bulk; a subset is spot-checked in docs/lightstim_capability_check.md with raw logs. Kept here as the full prompt set for later benchmarking runs.

categories.tool_build: Should invoke qec_circuit_build and report real numbers from it
categories.tool_edge_case: Should invoke qec_circuit_build (or fail schema validation) and report the failure gracefully, not a hand-rolled fallback
categories.tool_vs_corpus: Tests whether the model correctly distinguishes qec_circuit_build's LightStim-backed families from Stim-native code_params
categories.retrieval_paper: Corpus-only — should cite arxiv:2604.21472 and/or the ingested docs, no tool call needed
categories.retrieval_docs: Corpus-only — should cite github:QuTone/LightStim@47dd7497 (docs/api or skills), no tool call needed
categories.combined: Should both retrieve cited background and invoke the tool for a concrete number

prompts.question: Build a distance-3 toric code memory circuit and tell me its [[n,k,d]] and detector count.
I need a distance-6 BB code circuit — can you build it and tell me how many qubits and observables it has?
Construct a distance-3 PQRM code circuit for 3 rounds and report its qubit count and detector count.
I need a distance-5 color code circuit for 5 rounds — can you build it and diagram it?
prompts.notes: May also/instead invoke stim_diagram on the resulting circuit_text; color_code_666 is not LightStim-exclusive, see ls-cmp-002.

prompts.question: Build a distance-10 BB code memory circuit for 20 rounds.
Build a distance-7 BB code circuit.
prompts.expected_outcome: ok=False, error_message naming the supported bb_code presets {6, 10, 12}
prompts.notes: 7 is a valid distance value per schema but not a real BB preset.

prompts.question: Build a distance-4 color code circuit.
Build a distance-20 toric code circuit for 5 rounds.
prompts.expected_outcome: Pydantic validation error before the tool body runs — distance 20 is outside the tool's schema range [3, 15], not an ok=False payload.

prompts.question: Build a distance-6 BB code circuit for the 'distillation' protocol instead of memory.
prompts.expected_outcome: Rejected — protocol is a Literal["memory"], 'distillation' isn't accepted.

prompts.question: Compare a distance-3 surface code (Stim) against a distance-3 toric code (LightStim) — same physical error rate, which has more detectors?
How many physical qubits does a distance-3 color code have? I've seen different numbers in different tools — which is right?
prompts.notes: Tests whether the model explains the data-only vs data+ancilla convention difference rather than declaring one number wrong.

prompts.question: How does LightStim automate detector error model construction, and why does that matter compared to manual annotation?
What is the heterogeneous cross-code lattice surgery design LightStim demonstrates between surface and punctured quantum Reed-Muller codes?
What protocols does the LightStim paper benchmark, from memory experiments to end-to-end distillation circuits?
How did the LightStim authors cross-validate their detector and observable counts against public implementations?
What is the contract a new decoder must implement to be added to LightStim's decoder backend?
According to LightStim's own API docs, what does QECSystem provide over a single QECPatch?
What's the difference between LightStim's ExternalDecoder facade and writing a custom sinter.CompiledDecoder from scratch?
Explain LightStim's automated DEM construction approach, then build a distance-3 toric code circuit as a concrete example and report its detector count.
The LightStim paper mentions cross-validating logical error rates against public implementations — can you build a distance-6 BB code circuit so I can see its structure?
